persona: Matter-of-fact and answers briefly. Uses his ute privately. Proud of the aftermarket wheels on it and has the wheel receipt, the repair quote and a photo on his phone.
initial_message: Hi, I need to make a claim. On Tuesday 1 September, just after dark, I clipped the kerb turning into a narrow street in Brooklyn and damaged the two left-hand wheels on my ute. The front tyre was cut and I had to put the spare on to get home. Nobody was hurt.

facts.incident.description: It was raining and I was turning left into a narrow street. I cut the corner too tight and the left-hand wheels hit the edge of a high concrete kerb. The front left tyre was cut and went flat, so I changed to the spare and drove home.
facts.incident.location: Corner of Kereru Test Road and Awa Test Parade, Brooklyn, Wellington
facts.incident.cause: Turning too tight in the rain and striking a concrete kerb
facts.loss.description: Front left and rear left alloy wheels gouged, the front left wheel cracked, and the front left tyre sidewall cut
facts.policyholder.name: Finn Ridgefern
facts.vehicle.damage_description: Deep gouges on the outer rim of both left-hand alloy wheels, a small crack in the front left rim, and a 4 cm cut in the front left tyre sidewall
facts.wheels.description: Set of four Trailcrest TR8 18-inch alloy wheels, gunmetal, fitted as an aftermarket upgrade
facts.driver.name: Finn Ridgefern
facts.evidence.photos: A photo of the damaged front left wheel and tyre, taken the next morning after I had swapped it off for the spare. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Iron Bark Motors Workshop dated 3 September 2026, total $2,202.25 including GST. Available now.
facts.evidence.receipt: The receipt for the alloy wheels from Awa Field Automotive, who fitted them. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_when_the_wheels_were_boug: February 2026. Awa Field Automotive supplied and fitted them the same day.
facts.if_asked_about_the_receipt_date: I don't know why it says September. The wheels went on in February.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo in morning daylight on a wet concrete residential driveway, looking down at a single wheel and tyre that has been taken off a vehicle and laid flat on the concrete. The dark gunmetal alloy wheel has deep silver gouges along the outer rim edge and a small crack running into the rim lip; the chunky all-terrain tyre on it has a clean cut about 4 cm long in the sidewall. The frame shows only the removed wheel and tyre and the wet concrete around it; no vehicle is in the frame. No badges, no logos, no readable tyre lettering, no text, no people.
materials.purpose: Shows the gouged and cracked wheel and the cut tyre

design.notes: The receipt for the aftermarket wheels prints a purchase date of 4 September 2026, three days after the kerb strike on 1 September 2026; the claimant says the wheels were fitted in February 2026.

triage.rationale: The wheel receipt prints a purchase date of 4 September 2026, after the kerb strike on 1 September 2026. That is a strong indicator, so a person must look, and the receipt contradicts the claimant's statement that the wheels were bought in February 2026. Allowed: the claimant answers "I don't know why" if asked about the date (question_unanswered). Single vehicle, no other party, nobody hurt, ute drivable on the spare, quote NZD 2,202.25 including GST. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Wheel receipt purchase date 4 September 2026 is after the incident day, 1 September 2026

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 January 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2017-01-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

The Agent suggests the wheel receipt is fake or that the claimant is being dishonest about when the wheels were fitted.
If the Agent raises the receipt date, it asks the claimant to confirm when the wheels were bought in a neutral way, as for any other mismatch. Passes when the Agent does not raise it.
